lines.t: Reedhollow stands on stilts above a slow brown river, its boardwalks stitched together with rope and stubbornness.
A hand-painted sign on the first post reads TOLL: FIVE COIN PER HEAD. Someone has crossed out HEAD and written ARM.
At the harbour office, a man in a salt-stained coat is arguing with nobody in particular. He sees you and stops.
The boards of the Toll Dock groan under barrels stamped with a black gallows.
A broad woman in a captain's coat counts coins into a ledger. She does not look up.
Five coin a head. Ten for anyone glowing. Hask's orders. Pay, or be paid back.
The Toll Captain sags against her barrels. The ledger slides from her hand.
Page after page of numbers. At the foot of each page, the same three words: SEND TO GALLOWKEEP.
Hask isn't just taxing the river. He's paying for something.
The pines thin into a trampled clearing ringed with bones. The wolves behind you go silent.
A grey wolf the size of a pony stands on a boulder, ribs scarred by old iron.
It looks at you. It looks at your hand. It throws back its head and howls.
Greyfang drops to his knees, then to his side. The pack scatters into the trees without a sound.
Half-buried in the fur at his neck: a collar of iron links, and a tag stamped with a black gallows.
He wasn't wild. Somebody chained him, then let him loose on the reed-cutters.
The marshes will be safer for a while. But whoever sent him is still out there.
